name: SAMULE: Self-Learning Agents Enhanced by Multi-level Reflection
authors: Yubin Ge, Salvatore Romeo, Jason Cai, Monica Sunkara, Yi Zhang (AWS AI Labs / Amazon)
venue: EMNLP 2025 (Main Conference); Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Suzhou, China, pp. 16591-16610 (DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.emnlp-main.839)
reflection_type: learned-critic-model — a separate retrospective language model (Qwen 2.5 3B) is SFT-trained to generate trajectory-specific reflections; training-data reflections are synthesized via verbal self-critique against reference outputs across three granularities (micro/meso/macro). At inference, the trained retrospective model produces the verbal critique that guides the actor.
feedback_source: Hybrid. During offline reflection synthesis: ground-truth-oracle/reference (a valid reference plan ytrain) plus environment outcome (success/fail signal from official evaluation scripts / cost-calculation environment) and self-generated diagnoses. At inference, the trained retrospective model is self-contained and needs no reference; in the interactive setting feedback comes from comparing predicted vs. actual user/environment responses (foresight-based reflection).
iteration_structure: episodic-retry-with-reset — Reflexion-style trials (at most K, with K=4 trials at inference per Appendix A). Each failed trial yields a reflection appended to the next trial's context. In the interactive setting, foresight-based reflection triggers mid-interaction corrections at each turn.
reflection_object: action trajectory + reasoning chain — the retrospective model reflects on the agent's full ReAct trajectory (thought/action/observation steps) and produces a verbal diagnosis plus a revised high-level plan that is fed back as context (prompt augmentation). The underlying improvement artifact distilled is the reflection-generating model's weights (the retrospective model is SFT-trained), while the actor LLM itself is not weight-updated.
requires_training: SFT — the retrospective model (Qwen 2.5 3B) is trained via supervised fine-tuning (LoRA) on multi-level synthesized reflection data. No RL is used (the paper explicitly shows SFT beats the RL-based Retroformer variant). The actor LLM (Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet) is frozen / used only in-context.
reward_or_critic_model: separate retrospective model — a dedicated SFT-trained language model that generates reflections (critiques). No trained scalar reward model or RL critic is used; the reference output (oracle) and outcome success serve as the offline supervision signal for synthesizing the reflection targets.
distillation_target: model-weights — the synthesized multi-level reflections are distilled (via SFT) into the weights of a small retrospective model that generates reflections at inference. Secondarily, an error taxonomy (structured rules/notes) is built offline; but the inference-time learned artifact is the retrospective model's parameters.
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered — reflection is scaffolded via designed prompts and a hand-structured three-level synthesis pipeline (Single-Trajectory / Intra-Task / Inter-Task), with the reflective behavior then distilled into a model via SFT. It is not RL-emergent (no 'aha'-style emergence); it extends the Reflexion prompt-engineered lineage with a trained reflection generator.
memory_type: structured-notes/graph + long-term-episodic — an offline-constructed error taxonomy (a structured set of categorized error types) plus per-task/per-trajectory episodic reflections stored during synthesis. At inference the 'memory' is effectively parameterized inside the retrospective model; in the Reflexion-style loop, reflections are appended to context (scratchpad-style episodic buffer).
memory_persistence: cross-task — Inter-Task (macro) learning extracts transferable insights clustered across diverse task queries, and the trained retrospective model generalizes across tasks. Within a Reflexion trial loop, reflections persist cross-episode (across retries of the same task).
memory_curation_mechanism: self-summarized/curated — reflections from the three levels are merged via a final LLM summarization step into a single target reflection per trajectory; the error taxonomy is incrementally built (LLM checks the existing taxonomy and appends/merges new error types). The taxonomy is static after the offline phase (a stated limitation). Reference-based error classification filters which errors are retained.
error_localization_granularity: step-level (and multi-granular) — during Intra-Task (meso) learning the LLM labels each action step in a trajectory with an error type to obtain an 'error path', giving step-level localization. This rolls up to response/outcome-level (micro: whole-trajectory diagnosis vs. reference) and task-cluster-level (macro: errors grouped across tasks).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: both — explicitly spans intra-task (meso: error taxonomy across multiple trials of the SAME task query) and inter-task (macro: transferable insights from same-typed errors across DIFFERENT tasks), plus micro single-trajectory refinement. This three-level design is the paper's core contribution.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: both — non-interactive setting is avoidance-style (reflect after a failed trial, retry next episode, Reflexion-style); the interactive setting adds mid-trajectory recovery via foresight-based reflection that compares predicted vs. actual user response at each turn and corrects in-flight.
task_domains: decision-making / planning, tool-use, and dialogue — long-horizon agentic planning (travel planning, trip/meeting natural-language planning) and tool-agent-user interaction (retail and airline customer-service agents).
benchmarks: TravelPlanner; NATURAL PLAN (Trip Planning and Meeting Planning, excluding Calendar Scheduling); Tau-bench (Retail and Airline domains, both non-interactive and interactive). HotpotQA used in Appendix B for the Retroformer-variant validation.
headline_result: On TravelPlanner (Claude 3.5 Sonnet-v2 actor), SAMULE reaches 20.00% Pass Rate vs. 12.78% for the strongest baseline (Retroformer variant), 9.44% Inter-Task Error Reflection, 5.56% Reflexion, 4.44% ReAct, and 0.00% ExpeL — i.e., +7.22 points over the best baseline and ~3.6x Reflexion. With Claude 3.7 Sonnet, SAMULE reaches 29.44% vs. 21.67% (Retroformer variant).
baselines: ReAct; Reflexion; ExpeL; Inter-Task Error Reflection (static error-type reflections, an ablation of SAMULE itself); Retroformer variant (SFT + DPO replacing PPO, a memory-efficient re-implementation of Retroformer); Fewshot (for no-environment settings like NATURAL PLAN).
gains_vs_baseline: TravelPlanner (Claude 3.5 Sonnet-v2): SAMULE 20.00 vs. Retroformer variant 12.78 (+7.22). TravelPlanner (Claude 3.7 Sonnet): 29.44 vs. 21.67 (+7.77). NATURAL PLAN Trip (EM Accuracy): 60.31 vs. ExpeL 53.79 / Inter-Task 51.56 / Reflexion 50.00 (+6.52 over ExpeL). NATURAL PLAN Meeting: 48.50 vs. Retroformer variant 44.00 (+4.50). Tau-bench non-interactive (3 trials): Retail 87.83 vs. Reflexion 82.61 (+5.22), Airline 66.00 vs. 56.00 (+10.0). Tau-bench interactive: Retail 75.97 vs. Reflexion 69.75 (+6.22), Airline 55.32 vs. 48.50 (+6.82). Error reduction rate: SAMULE 0.67/0.73/0.53 vs. Reflexion 0.13/0.42/0.22 on TravelPlanner/NATURAL-PLAN-Trip/Meeting.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-time reflection model is lightweight (Qwen 2.5 3B); the actor runs Reflexion-style with up to 4 trials (so roughly up to 4x single-pass inference for the actor plus one retrospective-model call per failed trial). Retrospective-model training: LoRA + DeepSpeed Stage-3, AdamW, lr 5e-5, 15 epochs, batch size 1, on 8x NVIDIA A100, ~1 hour per run. The paper notes the offline multi-level reflection-synthesis phase (trajectory analysis, taxonomy construction, cross-task clustering) is resource-intensive for large/long-trajectory datasets, but it deliberately avoids costly/unstable RL (SFT-only), making training cheaper than the RL-based Retroformer.
known_limitations: (1) Static error taxonomy — built offline and fixed at inference, so it can become incomplete/outdated on new tasks or unseen failure patterns, limiting continual/lifelong learning. (2) Computational overhead in the offline multi-level reflection-synthesis phase (trajectory analysis, taxonomy construction, cross-task clustering) for large-scale datasets with long trajectories. (3) Dependence on a reference/valid output during training reflection synthesis, which is unavailable in some benchmarks (TravelPlanner uses the 'sole-setting' to keep trajectories tractable; full test set not used because outcomes can't be reflected on). (4) Over-providing the reference (at both micro and meso levels) actually degrades performance (15.56% vs. 20.00%).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: oracle-label/ground-truth (during training) + env-reward — reflection synthesis relies on a reference 'valid plan' (ytrain) and on success/fail outcomes from official evaluation scripts and the cost-calculation environment. At inference the retrospective model itself needs no reference, but the method's learning signal is fundamentally oracle/outcome-dependent. The ablation shows references are critical at the micro level (no-reference variant 18.33% vs. 20.00% with micro-only reference), confirming external/oracle feedback dependency.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive — improves consistently over reflection and non-reflection baselines across TravelPlanner, NATURAL PLAN, and Tau-bench, and over the RL-based Retroformer variant, in low-success/failure-dense regimes. Notably it does so without leaking labels at inference (reference used only offline for synthesis). The paper argues naive self-reflection (Reflexion/ExpeL) is insufficient under high task complexity (ExpeL collapses to 0% on TravelPlanner), whereas failure-centric, reference-grounded, multi-level synthesis yields robust gains.
calibration_effect: not-measured — the paper does not report confidence-calibration / overconfidence ('reasoning tax') metrics; it focuses on task pass/accuracy rates and an error-reduction-rate analysis rather than calibration.
failure_attribution_capability: classifies-failure-mode (taxonomy) + attributes-failing-step — the meso-level Intra-Task stage incrementally constructs an explicit error taxonomy and classifies the error type of each action step (producing an 'error path' with per-step critiques/rationales), and the macro level clusters trajectories by shared error type across tasks.
failure_mode_addressed: Domain-specific planning/agent error types rather than MAST's multi-agent taxonomy. The constructed TravelPlanner taxonomy includes ~26 categories, e.g. Budget Constraint Violation, Accommodation Minimum Stay Violation, Accommodation Capacity/Child/Pet/Smoking/Party Policy Violations, Travel Time Scheduling/Planning Error, Restaurant Selection/Timing Error, Transportation Planning/Cost Error, Location Verification Error, Geographic Data Misinterpretation, Query Requirement Mismatch, Incomplete Day Planning, Inefficient Resource Allocation. Conceptually it targets MAST-style 'superficial self-reflection' / inadequate error analysis by replacing generic reflections with diagnosed, step-level, reference-grounded error feedback.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset or benchmark released; the work uses existing benchmarks (TravelPlanner, NATURAL PLAN, Tau-bench, HotpotQA). It does synthesize multi-level reflection training data and an error taxonomy, but no public release of these artifacts is documented. [uncertain whether synthesized data is released]
builds_on: Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023; verbal reinforcement / self-reflection loop, base structure); ReAct (Yao et al. 2023; base planning algorithm); Retroformer (Yao et al. 2024b; retrospective model trained with policy-gradient/PPO — SAMULE's closest predecessor, replacing RL with reference-grounded multi-level SFT); ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024; experiential learning from successful trajectories — critiqued as success-reliant); CTRL (Xie et al. 2025; RL-based critique); contrastive retrospection (Sun et al. 2023); Kolb's experiential learning cycle (educational-psychology motivation).
extended_by_or_inspired: As an October-2025 EMNLP paper it is too recent for established successors. A closely related contemporaneous AWS Labs project, CLEAR (Contrastive Learning of Experience via Agentic Reflection; awslabs/CLEAR), trains a Context Augmentation Model via reflection-distilled SFT then RL — same research lineage/group direction. citation_count: 8 (Semantic Scholar, as of June 2026; CorpusId 281525659, DBLP conf/emnlp/GeRCSZ25)
reasoning_model_native: no — SAMULE targets standard (non-reasoning-native) instruction-tuned actors (Claude 3.5 Sonnet-v2, Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and adds reflection externally via a separately trained retrospective model. It does not rely on or specifically study o1/R1-style built-in reflection; reflection is scaffolded/distilled rather than native.
on_policy_distillation_link: Related but off-policy-leaning. Reflection targets are synthesized using the strong actor (Claude 3.5 Sonnet-v2) and oracle references, then distilled via SFT into a small retrospective model (Qwen 2.5 3B) — a form of skill/critique distillation. It is not on-policy distillation in the strict RL sense (no online policy rollouts updating the actor; the actor stays frozen and only its context is improved). The RL baseline (Retroformer variant, SFT+DPO/PPO) is the closer on-policy analogue, which SAMULE deliberately replaces with SFT.
sample_efficiency: Training run is highly efficient: ~1 hour on 8x A100 (LoRA, 15 epochs) for the 3B retrospective model, with SFT-only (no rollout-heavy RL). Data is synthesized from up to K=4 retry trials per training task. At inference, up to 4 trials per task. The paper frames SFT-on-good-reflections as more sample/compute-efficient and more stable than RL, but does not report a formal trials-to-target sample-efficiency curve beyond per-trial performance plots (Figure 2).
